title: immunarch
text: immunarch brings comprehensive analytics toolkit build reproducible analysis pipelines Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoire (AIRR) data particular focus designing personalized immunotherapies vaccines. Key features : Multi-modal immune profiling: compute receptor- repertoire-level statistics leveraging single-cell, spatial, immunogenicity receptor annotations; Immunomics scale: work seamlessly datasets don’t fit memory; Immune biomarker discovery: stratify cohorts timepoints, derive repertoire signatures (diversity/clonality, V/J usage, similarity), track antigen-annotated clonotypes; Feature engineering: build Machine Learning-ready feature tables (receptor-, ssample- cohort-level) core repertoire metrics annotations, consistent IDs/metadata downstream statistics modeling; Modular, extendable, adaptable: add new analyses metrics via extension API, use adapters interoperate AIRR tools formats.

title: BCR
text: B-cell receptor (BCR) consists immunoglobulin molecule СD79 molecule. BCR includes two identical heavy chains (generated recombination V, D, J segments), two identical light chains (generated recombination V J segments). Rapid improvements high-throughput sequencing provide opportunity study B-cell immunoglobulin receptors cell surface [1] via process called BCR repertoire sequencing. pipeline describes work BCR repertoire data preprocessing raw sequenced data MiXCR (https://docs.milaboratories.com/mixcr//) programs. pipeline involves five steps: Data loading. step includes loading data checking whether enough information pipeline work. Reconstructing clonal lineages. step, BCR sequences divided clonal lineages — sets sequences presumably share common ancestor. Building germline. step, algorithm generates sequence represents ancestral sequence BCR clonal lineage. Aligning sequences within clonal lineages. step involves preparation phylogenetic somatic hypermutation analysis. Phylogenetic analysis. step provides phylogeny reconstruction trunk length calculation (running PHYLIP package). Somatic hypermutation analysis. step, compare clonotype germline sequences detect count number mutations clonotype sequence.

Immunarch package, function repAlignLineage aligns sequences within clonal lineages. function requires Clustal W app installed. app downloaded : http://www.clustal.org/download/current/, installed via system package manager (apt dnf). Ubuntu, check guide: https://www.howtoinstall./ubuntu/18-04/clustalw/ Windows, download run clustalw-x.x-win.msi repAlignLineage usage example: function several parameters: .min_lineage_sequences — Filters clusters (clonal lineages) number clonotypes lower threshold. Aligning clonal lineages sequences little use. .prepare_threads — number threads prepare results table. high number can cause memory overload! .align_threads — number threads lineage alignment. Align sequences cluster can visualized using standard functions:
code: sudo apt update sudo apt install clustalw data(bcrdata) bcr_data <- bcrdata$data %>% top(500) bcr_data %>%   seqCluster(seqDist(bcr_data), .fixed_threshold = 3) %>%   repGermline(.threads = 1) %>%   repAlignLineage(.min_lineage_sequences = 2) # take clusters that contain at least 1 sequence bcr_data <- bcrdata$data align_dt <- bcr_data %>%   seqCluster(seqDist(bcr_data, .col = 'CDR3.nt', .group_by_seqLength = TRUE),              .perc_similarity = 0.6) %>%   repGermline(.threads = 1) %>%   repAlignLineage(.min_lineage_sequences = 6, .align_threads = 2, .nofail = TRUE) # A name of the first cluster align_dt$full_clones$Cluster[[1]]  # Alignment of sequences from the first cluster image(align_dt$full_clones$Alignment[[1]], grid = TRUE)

text: BCR phylogenetic analysis, use maximum parsimony method. maximum parsimony method reconstructs phylogenetic tree lineage minimizing total number mutation events [2]. method also enables reconstruction intermediate sequences may existed BCR germline sequence. simulated sequences contain mutations ancestral clonotype group selected maximum parsimony analysis. Immunarch, function repClonalFamily builds phylogeny B-cells, generates common ancestor, calculates trunk length. mean trunk length represents distance recent common ancestor germline sequence [3]. Mean trunk length serves measure maturity lineage. trunk length lineage tree approximates maturation state initiating B cell clone [4]. function requires PHYLIP app installed. app can downloaded : https://evolution.genetics.washington.edu/phylip/getme-new1.html, installed system package manager (apt dnf). Ubuntu, follow installation guide (https://zoomadmin.com/HowToInstall/UbuntuPackage/phylip ): Download Zip archive (https://evolution.genetics.washington.edu/phylip/install.html). Extract archive folder. Add folder PATH (https://www.architectryan.com/2018/03/17/add---path--windows-10/) repClonalFamily usage example: cluster tree represented table (default number clones CommonAncestor, Germline, Presumable 1): can recolor leaves. example, recolor leaves number AA mutations 0: Another way recolor leaves use .vis_groups parameter repClonalFamily. allows assign group names specific clone IDs, lists clone IDs: found 4 clusters: found mismatches germline ancestor sequence. Dots represent nucleotides matches sequences, letters represent mismatches sequences: calculated trunk length cluster: Also trunk length specified “TreeStats” table column “DistanceNT”.
code: sudo apt-get update -y sudo apt-get install -y phylip bcr <- align_dt %>%   repClonalFamily(.threads = 2, .nofail = TRUE) #plot visualization of the first tree vis(bcr[["full_clones"]][["TreeStats"]][[1]]) #example for the first tree bcr[["full_clones"]][["TreeStats"]][[1]] #take sequence where number of AA mutations is not 0 f <- bcr[["full_clones"]][["TreeStats"]][[1]] #rename these leaves f[f$DistanceAA != 0, ]['Type'] = 'mutationAA' #new tree vis(f) #get all clone IDs from align_dt clone_ids <- unnest(align_dt[["full_clones"]], "Sequences")[["Clone.ID"]] #run repClonalFamily with assigning some of these clones to differently named and colored groups bcr_with_groups <- align_dt %>%   repClonalFamily(.vis_groups = list(                     Group1 = clone_ids[1],                     Group2 = clone_ids[3],                     Group3 = list(clone_ids[5], clone_ids[2]),                     Group4 = c(clone_ids[7], clone_ids[4])                    ), .threads = 2, .nofail = TRUE                  ) #display the first tree from repClonalFamily results vis(bcr_with_groups[["full_clones"]][["TreeStats"]][[1]]) bcr$full_clones$Cluster %>% unique() # the example of common ancestor sequence bcr$full_clones$Common.Ancestor[1]  # the example of mismatches between a germline and an ancestor sequence bcr$full_clones$Germline.Output[1] bcr$full_clones[ , c('Cluster', 'Trunk.Length') ] #example fot first tree bcr[["full_clones"]][["TreeStats"]][[1]][1, ]

Each table has corresponding name from the DATA for (i in seq_along(DATA)) {   DBI::dbWriteTable(con, names(DATA)[i], DATA[[i]], overwrite = TRUE) }  # Create a source in the temporary directory with MonetDB ms <- MonetDBLite::src_monetdblite(dbdir = dbdir) res_db <- list()  # Load the data from MonetDB to dplyr tables for (i in seq_along(DATA)) {   res_db[[names(DATA)[i]]] <- dplyr::tbl(ms, names(DATA)[i]) }  # Your data is ready to use list(data = res_db, meta = META)

title: Data loading
text: immunarch comes data format, including tab-delimited columns can specified follows: “Clones” - count number barcodes (events, UMIs) reads; “Proportion” - proportion barcodes (events, UMIs) reads; “CDR3.nt” - CDR3 nucleotide sequence; “CDR3.aa” - CDR3 amino acid sequence; “V.name” - names aligned Variable gene segments; “D.name” - names aligned Diversity gene segments NA; “J.name” - names aligned Joining gene segments; “V.end” - last positions aligned V gene segments (1-based); “D.start” - positions D’5 end aligned D gene segments (1-based); “D.end” - positions D’3 end aligned D gene segments (1-based); “J.start” - first positions aligned J gene segments (1-based); “VJ.ins” - number inserted nucleotides (N-nucleotides) V-J junction (-1 receptors VDJ recombination); “VD.ins” - number inserted nucleotides (N-nucleotides) V-D junction (-1 receptors VJ recombination); “DJ.ins” - number inserted nucleotides (N-nucleotides) D-J junction (-1 receptors VJ recombination); “Sequence” - full nucleotide sequence.

title: Loading MiXCR Data
text: Follow instructions install MiXCR get started processing data. Important Note: Currently supports MiXCR version 3 . MiXCR supports following formats sequencing data: fasta, fastq, fastq.gz, paired-end fastq fastq.gz. tutorial use real IGH data . can choose use analyze amplicon method process one go: execute step align, assemble, exportClones individually.
code: mixcr analyze amplicon --species hs \       --starting-material dna \       --5-end v-primers \       --3-end j-primers \       --adapters adapters-present \       --receptor-type IGH \       input_R1.fastq input_R2.fastq analysis > mixcr align -s hs -OvParameters.geneFeatureToAlign=VTranscript \   --report analysis.report input_R1.fastq input_R2.fastq analysis.vdjca  Analysis Date: Mon Aug 25 15:22:39 MSK 2014 Input file(s): input_r1.fastq,input_r2.fastq Output file: alignments.vdjca Command line arguments: align --report alignmentReport.log input_r1.fastq input_r2.fastq alignments.vdjca Total sequencing reads: 323248 Successfully aligned reads: 210360 Successfully aligned, percent: 65.08% Alignment failed because of absence of V hits: 4.26% Alignment failed because of absence of J hits: 30.19% Alignment failed because of low total score: 0.48%

title: Loading MiXCR Data
text: run commands, generate files detailed information calculated clonotypes: Create new folder contains specified clonotype text files runs, create metadata.txt file following format. metadata file “metadata.txt” tab delimited file first column named “Sample” number additional columns arbitrary names. first column contain base names files without extensions folder. next section explain load single file multiple samples folder.
code: . ├── analysis.clonotypes.<chains>.txt <-- This contains the count data we want! ├── analysis.clna <- Build clonotypes correct PCR and sequencing errors ├── analysis.vdjca <- Align raw sequences to reference sequences of segments (V, D, J) of IGH gene ├── analysis.report <- Information on the run

title: Data Filtering
text: many research cases, want filter data metadata, clonotypes parameters genes, purpose, can use repFilter function.

title: Data Filtering
text: repFilter 3 parameters: .method, .query .match. Due ambiguity ways extract required data, repFilter following methods: .method = ".meta" - filters data using information meta data. .method = ".repertoire" ".rep" - filters data using information repertoire statistics. .method = ".clonotype" ".cl" - filters data using information clonotype sequences. Parameter .query list specifying condition filtering. Elements list conditions, names elements - columns chosen filtering. Names elements repeated .query. need write complex condition, can call function multiple times. Parameter .match denotes type match condition value filter: exact - looks exact match. substring- looks substring. startswith - looks string starting pattern Parameter .match can applied .meta .clonotype Load package R environment: testing purposes use scdata immdata datasets Immunarch library. Load executing following command: Look meta data immdata datasets:
code: library(immunarch) data(immdata) # look at the metadata immdata$meta ## # A tibble: 12 × 6 ##    Sample  ID    Sex     Age Status Lane  ##    <chr>   <chr> <chr> <dbl> <chr>  <chr> ##  1 A2-i129 C1    M        11 C      A     ##  2 A2-i131 C2    M         9 C      A     ##  3 A2-i133 C4    M        16 C      A     ##  4 A2-i132 C3    F         6 C      A     ##  5 A4-i191 C8    F        22 C      B     ##  6 A4-i192 C9    F        24 C      B     ##  7 MS1     MS1   M        12 MS     C     ##  8 MS2     MS2   M        30 MS     C     ##  9 MS3     MS3   M         8 MS     C     ## 10 MS4     MS4   F        14 MS     C     ## 11 MS5     MS5   F        15 MS     C     ## 12 MS6     MS6   F        15 MS     C # look at samples name in data names(immdata$data) ##  [1] "A2-i129" "A2-i131" "A2-i133" "A2-i132" "A4-i191" "A4-i192" "MS1"     ##  [8] "MS2"     "MS3"     "MS4"     "MS5"     "MS6"

title: Data Filtering

title: Data Filtering
text: Use interval, lessthan(minus infinity value) morethan(value plus infinity) define interval values filter statement. options accept float. lessthan morethan include borders interval includes left border excludes right border. Filter samples Age lower 23: Filter samples Age upper 15: Filter samples Age 15 23: can also use multiple conditions. case, function returns values matches conditions (logical operator) Filter samples Age 15 23 Lane B : Filter samples Age 15 23 Lane B:

title: Repertoire overlap and public clonotypes
text: Repertoire overlap common approach measure repertoire similarity. achieved computation specific statistics clonotypes shared given repertoires, also called “public” clonotypes. immunarch provides several indices: - number public clonotypes (.method = "public") - classic measure overlap similarity. overlap coefficient (.method = "overlap") - normalised measure overlap similarity. defined size intersection divided smaller size two sets. Jaccard index (.method = "jaccard") - measures similarity finite sample sets, defined size intersection divided size union sample sets. Tversky index (.method = "tversky") - asymmetric similarity measure sets compares variant prototype. using default arguments, ’s similar Dice’s coefficient. cosine similarity (.method = "cosine") - measure similarity two non-zero vectors Morisita’s overlap index (.method = "morisita") - statistical measure dispersion individuals population. used compare overlap among samples. incremental overlap - overlaps N abundant clonotypes incrementally growing N (.method = "inc+METHOD", e.g., "inc+public" "inc+morisita"). function includes described methods repOverlap. , output easily visualised passed vis() function work:   can easily change number significant digits:  analyse computed overlap measures function apply repOverlapAnalysis.

Feel free change "exc" case data formats. default, recommend leave way. .ambig = "exc" - filters clonotypes ambiguous gene alignments. .ambig = "wei" - introduces weighted approach (divides n (1/n) frequency entry corresponding gene n genes clonotype). .ambig = "maj" - chooses first gene segment.

title: Gene usage analysis
text: analyse gene usage immunarch introduces geneUsageAnalysis function. .method parameter controls data going preprocessed analysed. geneUsageAnalysis includes following methods preprocessing: “js” - Jensen-Shannon Divergence. “cor” - correlation. “cosine” - cosine similarity. “pca” - principal component analysis. “mds” - multi-dimensional scaling. “tsne” - t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding. methods actual analysis: “hclust” - clusters data using hierarchical clustering. “kmeans” - clusters data using K-means. “dbscan” - clusters data using DBSCAN. “kruskall” - compute Kruskall gene separately data splitted groups (without preprocessing). Results used Dunn test order detect significant differences groups. can call several methods single line code, probably powerful feature package. instance, "js+hclust" first computes Jensen-Shannon divergence applies hierarchical clustering resulting distance matrix, whereas "anova" computes ANOVA gene separately repertoires grouped:  Now let us visualise output preprocessing analysis:  top can add clustering:  can regulate number clusters well:
code: imm_gu <- geneUsage(immdata$data, "hs.trbv", .norm = T)  imm_gu_js <- geneUsageAnalysis(imm_gu, .method = "js", .verbose = F) imm_gu_cor <- geneUsageAnalysis(imm_gu, .method = "cor", .verbose = F)  p1 <- vis(imm_gu_js, .title = "Gene usage JS-divergence", .leg.title = "JS", .text.size = 1.5) p2 <- vis(imm_gu_cor, .title = "Gene usage correlation", .leg.title = "Cor", .text.size = 1.5)  p1 + p2 imm_gu_js[is.na(imm_gu_js)] <- 0  vis(geneUsageAnalysis(imm_gu, "cosine+hclust", .verbose = F)) # vis(geneUsageAnalysis(imm_gu, "js+dbscan", .verbose = F)) imm_cl_pca <- geneUsageAnalysis(imm_gu, "js+pca+kmeans", .verbose = F) imm_cl_mds <- geneUsageAnalysis(imm_gu, "js+mds+kmeans", .verbose = F) imm_cl_tsne <- geneUsageAnalysis(imm_gu, "js+tsne+kmeans", .perp = .01, .verbose = F) ## Perplexity should be lower than K! p1 <- vis(imm_cl_pca, .plot = "clust") p2 <- vis(imm_cl_mds, .plot = "clust") p3 <- vis(imm_cl_tsne, .plot = "clust") p1 + p2 + p3 imm_cl_pca2 <- geneUsageAnalysis(imm_gu, "js+pca+kmeans", .k = 3, .verbose = F) vis(imm_cl_pca2)

text: visualise k-mer statistics, vis() function comes help:  vis() function k-mers number arguments manipulate plot. First, .head argument specifies number abundant k-mers visualise.  Second, three options choose positions bars: “stack”, “dodge” “fill”, adjusted providing correposnding option .position argument:  Option “stack” stacks bars top can see full distribution k-mers. text: immunarch utilises common approaches sequence motif analysis uses different types matrices represent sequence motifs: position frequency matrix (PFM) - matrix occurences amino acid position; position probability matrix (PPM) - matrix probabilities occurences amino acid position; position weight matrix (PWM) - matrix log likelihoods PPM elements; matrix self-information elements PWM. compute visualise sequence motifs, first need compute k-mer statistics one input immune repertoires, apply kmer_profile() function compute sequence motif matrices: Currently support sequence motifs analysis one sample, working including following release. order compute visualise sequence motif matrices samples need process one one, can easily done -loops via lapply() function. Argument .method specifies matrix compute: .method = "freq" - position frequency matrix (PFM); .method = "prob" - position probability matrix (PPM); .method = "wei" - position weight matrix (PWM); .method = "self" - self-information matrix.

what: Clonality - receptor overabundance statistics for immune repertoires — airr_clonality
title: Clonality - receptor overabundance statistics for immune repertoires — airr_clonality
text: family functions quantify receptor overabundance per repertoire. Helps deciphering structure partition repertoire. airr_clonality_line - build ranked abundance lines: repertoire, take top limit receptors count attach repertoire metadata. Useful per-repertoire rank-abundance plots. airr_clonality_rank - aggregate clonal space rank bins. Receptors ordered proportion within repertoire; receptor assigned smallest threshold bins contains rank. airr_clonality_prop - aggregate clonal space proportion bins. receptor assigned named bin according proportion (e.g., Hyperexpanded >= 1e-2, Large >= 1e-3, ...). Thresholds matched descending order; unmatched receptors fall "Ultra-rare".

what: Diversity - estimating the heterogeneity of immune repertoires — airr_diversity
title: Diversity - estimating the heterogeneity of immune repertoires — airr_diversity
text: family functions quantify receptor diversity per repertoire. characteristic whole repertoire. airr_diversity_dxx - coverage diversity: minimal number top receptors needed reach perc% clonal space (proportion). Great spotting dominance/overexpansion quick, interpretable dashboards (e.g., D50 = receptors cover half repertoire). airr_diversity_chao1 - Chao1 estimator nonparameteric asymptotic estimator species richness (number species population). One used methods estimating immune repertoire diversity. airr_diversity_shannon - Shannon entropy (base 2) per repertoire computed proportion. Ideal want single evenness-aware diversity score; pair Pielou/Hill samples different richness. airr_diversity_pielou - Pielou's evenness H / log2(S) richness S. Best need size-normalized evenness score comparable across repertoires different receptor counts. airr_diversity_index - convenience alias Hill number q = 1 (exp(Shannon) using natural log). solid default single metric relatively robust rare-count noise easy compare across samples. airr_diversity_hill - Hill numbers ("true diversity") orders q \eqn{\}{} {0, 1, 2, ...}: q=0 richness, q=1 exp(Shannon), q>1 emphasizes abundant receptors. Perfect want diversity profile tunes sensitivity rare vs. abundant clonotypes.

what: Compute key immune repertoire statistics — airr_stats
title: Compute key immune repertoire statistics — airr_stats
text: family functions extract core descriptive statistics ImmunData object. airr_stats_chains — count V(D)J chains per repertoire (optionally split locus). Quickly gauges capture depth per repertoire , split locus, reveals TRA/TRB/IGH balance. Use QC, library-size checks, spot locus-specific dropouts -representation. airr_stats_lengths — count number sequence lengths per repertoire. Summarizes CDR3 length distribution, sensitive QC fingerprint repertoire prep selection. Helpful detecting primer/UMI biases, comparing cohorts, deriving length-based features models. airr_stats_genes - count V(D)J gene segments per repertoire, optionally split locus using either receptor counts barcode/UMI counts measure. Profiles V/D/J gene usage characterize repertoire composition germline biases, optional locus split. Useful cohort comparisons, flagging clonal expansions, producing ML-ready features repertoire-level ML tasks.

title: Compute key immune repertoire statistics — airr_stats
text: idata ImmunData object. locus_col Column idata$annotations stores locus (e.g. "locus"). NULL missing, result split locus. autojoin Logical. TRUE, join repertoire metadata schema repertoire id. Change default behaviour calling options(immunarch.autojoin = FALSE). format String. One "long" ("long" tibble imd_repertoire_id, facet columns, value; useful visualizations) "wide" (wide/unmelted table features, row corresponding specific repertoire / pair repertoires; useful Machine Learning). seq_col Character vector names columns containing sequences. gene_col single column name idata$annotations gene segment calls (e.g., "v_call", "d_call", "j_call", "c_call"). Default "v_call". level One "receptor" "barcode". "receptor" (default), function counts unique receptors (one per receptor ID) carry given gene segment. "barcode", function sums counts (e.g., cells/UMIs) per gene segment using column defined immundata::imd_schema("count"). Either NULL (split) "locus". "locus", result split locus column present (given immundata::imd_schema("locus")); otherwise warning emitted split ignored.

title: Main function for data filtering — repFilter
text: .data data processed. Must list 2 elements: data table metadata table. .method Method filtering. Implemented methods: .meta, .repertoire (.rep), .clonotype (.cl) Default value: '.clonotype'. .query Filtering query. named list filters applied data. Possible values names list dependent filter methods: .meta: filters metadata. Names named list metadata column headers. .repertoire: filters number clonotypes total number clones sample. Possible names named list "n_clonotypes" "n_clones". .clonotype: filters data samples. Names named list data column headers. Elements named list filters filtering options. Possible values filtering options: include("STR1", "STR2", ...): keeps rows matching values. Available methods: ".meta", ".clonotype". exclude("STR1", "STR2", ...): removes rows matching values. Available methods: ".meta", ".clonotype". lessthan(value): keeps rows/samples numeric values less specified. Available methods: ".meta", ".repertoire", ".clonotype". morethan(value): keeps rows/samples numeric values specified. Available methods: ".meta", ".repertoire", ".clonotype". interval(, ): keeps rows/samples numeric values fits interval. inclusive, exclusive. Available methods: ".meta", ".repertoire", ".clonotype". Default value: 'list(CDR3.aa = exclude("partial", "out_of_frame"))'. .match Matching method "include" "exclude" options query. Possible values: exact: matches exact specified string; startswith: matches strings starting specified substring; substring: matches strings containing specified substring. Default value: 'exact'.

what: Creates germlines for clonal lineages — repGermline
title: Creates germlines for clonal lineages — repGermline
text: function creates germlines clonal lineages. B cell clonal lineage represents set B cells presumably common origin (arising VDJ rearrangement event) common ancestor. clonal lineage germline sequence represents ancestral sequence BCR clonal lineage. words, germline sequence sequence B-cells immediately VDJ recombination, B-cell maturation hypermutation process. Germline sequence useful assessing degree mutation maturity repertoire.

title: Creates germlines for clonal lineages — repGermline
code: repGermline(.data, .species, .min_nuc_outside_cdr3, .threads)

title: Creates germlines for clonal lineages — repGermline
text: .data data processed. Can data.frame, data.table::data.table list objects. must columns immunarch compatible format immunarch_data_format. .species Species data acquired. Available options: "HomoSapiens" (default), "MusMusculus", "BosTaurus", "CamelusDromedarius", "CanisLupusFamiliaris", "DanioRerio", "MacacaMulatta", "MusMusculusDomesticus", "MusMusculusCastaneus", "MusMusculusMolossinus", "MusMusculusMusculus", "MusSpretus", "OncorhynchusMykiss", "OrnithorhynchusAnatinus", "OryctolagusCuniculus", "RattusNorvegicus", "SusScrofa". .min_nuc_outside_cdr3 parameter sets many nucleotides V J chain outside CDR3 considered good alignment. .threads Number threads use.

title: Creates germlines for clonal lineages — repGermline
text: Data added columns: Sequence (FR1+CDR1+FR2+CDR2+FR3+CDR3+FR4 nucleotides; column replaced exists) V.allele, J.allele (chosen alleles V J genes), V.aa, J.aa (V J sequences original clonotype, outside CDR3, converted amino acids) Germline.sequence (combined germline nucleotide sequence)

what: Load immune repertoire files into the R workspace — repLoad
title: Load immune repertoire files into the R workspace — repLoad
text: repLoad function loads repertoire files R workspace immunarch format can immediately use analysis. repLoad automatically detects right format files, need simply provide path files. See "Details" information supported formats. See "Examples" diving right .

title: Load immune repertoire files into the R workspace — repLoad
code: repLoad(.path, .mode = "paired", .coding = TRUE, ...)

title: Load immune repertoire files into the R workspace — repLoad
text: .path character string specifying path input data. Input data can one following: single repertoire file. case repLoad returns R data.frame; vector paths repertoire files. case metadata file presented next section ; path folder repertoire files , available, metadata file "metadata.txt". metadata file presented, repLoad returns list two elements "data" "meta". "data" another list repertoire R data.frames. "meta" data frame metadata. metadata file "metadata.txt" presented, repLoad creates dummy metadata file sample names returns list two elements "data" "meta". input data multiple chains cell types stored file (example, like 10xGenomics repertoire files), repertoire files splitted different R data frames one type chain cell presented. metadata file additional columns specifying cell chain types different samples. .mode Either "single" single chain data "paired" paired chain data. Currently "single" works every format, "paired" works 10X Genomics data. default, 10X Genomics data loaded paired chain data, files loaded single chain data. .coding logical value. Set TRUE get coding-clonotypes (defaul). Set FALSE get clonotypes. ... Extra arguments parsing functions

title: Load immune repertoire files into the R workspace — repLoad
text: list two named elements: "data" list input samples; "meta" data frame sample metadata.

title: Load immune repertoire files into the R workspace — repLoad
text: metadata tab delimited file first column named "Sample". can number additional columns arbitrary names. first column contain base names files without extensions folder. Example: Currently, Immunarch support following formats: "immunoseq" - ImmunoSEQ version. http://www.adaptivebiotech.com/immunoseq "mitcr" - MiTCR. https://github.com/milaboratory/mitcr "mixcr" - MiXCR ("" files) version. https://github.com/milaboratory/mixcr "migec" - MiGEC. http://migec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ "migmap" - parsing IgBLAST results postprocessed MigMap. https://github.com/mikessh/migmap "tcr" - tcR, previous package. https://imminfo.github.io/tcr/ "vdjtools" - VDJtools version. http://vdjtools-doc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ "imgt" - IMGT HighV-QUEST. http://www.imgt.org/HighV-QUEST/ "airr" - adaptive immune receptor repertoire (AIRR) data format. http://docs.airr-community.org/en/latest/datarep/overview.html "10x" - 10XGenomics clonotype annotations tables. https://support.10xgenomics.com/single-cell-vdj/software/pipelines/latest/output/annotation "archer" - ArcherDX clonotype tables. https://archerdx.com/

what: Main function for public clonotype statistics calculations — repOverlap
title: Main function for public clonotype statistics calculations — repOverlap
text: repOverlap function designed analyse overlap two repertoires. contains number methods compare immune receptor sequences shared individuals.

title: Main function for public clonotype statistics calculations — repOverlap
code: repOverlap(   .data,   .method = c("public", "overlap", "jaccard", "tversky", "cosine", "morisita",     "inc+public", "inc+morisita"),   .col = "aa",   .a = 0.5,   .b = 0.5,   .verbose = TRUE,   .step = 1000,   .n.steps = 10,   .downsample = FALSE,   .bootstrap = NA,   .verbose.inc = NA,   .force.matrix = FALSE )

title: Main function for public clonotype statistics calculations — repOverlap
text: .data data processed. Can data.frame, data.table::data.table, list objects. Every object must columns immunarch compatible format. immunarch_data_format Competent users may provide advanced data representations: DBI database connections, list objects. supported limitations basic objects. Note: connection must represent separate repertoire. .method string specifies method analysis combination methods. repOverlap function supports following basic methods: "public", "overlap", "jaccard", "tversky", "cosine", "morisita". vector multiple methods given parameter, first method used. .col string specifies column(s) processed. Pass one following strings, separated plus sign: "nt" nucleotide sequences, "aa" amino acid sequences, "v" V gene segments, "j" J gene segments. E.g., pass "aa+v" compute overlaps CDR3 amino acid sequences paired V gene segments, .e., case unique clonotype pair CDR3 amino acid V gene segment. Clonal counts equal clonotypes summed . ., .b Alpha beta parameters Tversky Index. Default values give Jaccard index measure. .verbose TRUE output progress. .step Either integer numeric vector. first case, integer defines step incremental overlap. second case, vector encodes repertoire sampling depths. .n.steps Skipped ".step" numeric vector. .downsample TRUE performs downsampling N clonotypes step instead choosing top N clonotypes incremental overlaps. Change nothing using conventional methods. .bootstrap Set NA turn bootstrapping, set number perform bootstrapping number tries. .verbose.inc Logical. TRUE shows output computation process. .force.matrix Logical. TRUE always forces matrix output even case two input repertoires.

title: Main function for public clonotype statistics calculations — repOverlap
text: cases return value matrix overlap values pair repertoires. two repertoires provided, return value single numeric value. one incremental method chosen, return list overlap matrix.

title: Main function for public clonotype statistics calculations — repOverlap
text: "public" "shared" synonyms exist convenience researchers. "overlap" coefficient similarity measure measures overlap two finite sets. "jaccard" index conceptually percentage many objects two sets common many objects total. "tversky" index asymmetric similarity measure sets compares variant prototype. "cosine" index measure similarity two non-zero vectors inner product space measures cosine angle . title: Track clonotypes across time and data points — trackClonotypes
text: .data data process. can data.frame, data.table::data.table, list objects. Every object must columns immunarch compatible format. immunarch_data_format Competent users may provide advanced data representations: DBI database connections, list objects. supported limitations basic objects. Note: connection must represent separate repertoire. .argument regulates clonotypes choose tracking. three options argument: passes list two elements list(X, Y), X name index target repertoire ".data", Y number abundant clonotypes take X. passes character vector sequences take data frames; passes data frame (data table, database) one columns - first sequences, gene segments (applicable). See "Examples" examples option. .col character vector length 1. Specifies identifier column, function chooses clonotype sequences. Specify "nt" nucleotide sequences, "aa" amino acid sequences, "aa+v" amino acid sequences Variable genes, "nt+j" nucleotide sequences Joining genes, combination . Used "." option 1) option 2). .norm Logical. TRUE uses Proportion instead number Clones per clonotype store function output.

code: # Load an example data that comes with immunarch data(immdata)  # Make the data smaller in order to speed up the examples immdata$data <- immdata$data[c(1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9)] immdata$meta <- immdata$meta[c(1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9), ]  # Option 1 # Choose the first 10 amino acid clonotype sequences # from the first repertoire to track tc <- trackClonotypes(immdata$data, list(1, 10), .col = "aa") # Choose the first 20 nucleotide clonotype sequences # and their V genes from the "MS1" repertoire to track tc <- trackClonotypes(immdata$data, list("MS1", 20), .col = "nt+v")  # Option 2 # Choose clonotypes with amino acid sequences "CASRGLITDTQYF" or "CSASRGSPNEQYF" tc <- trackClonotypes(immdata$data, c("CASRGLITDTQYF", "CSASRGSPNEQYF"), .col = "aa")  # Option 3 # Choose the first 10 clonotypes from the first repertoire # with amino acid sequences and V segments target <- immdata$data[[1]] %>%   select(CDR3.aa, V.name) %>%   head(10) tc <- trackClonotypes(immdata$data, target)  # Visualise the output regardless of the chosen option # Therea are three way to visualise it, regulated by the .plot argument vis(tc, .plot = "smooth") #> Warning: id.vars and measure.vars are internally guessed when both are 'NULL'. All non-numeric/integer/logical type columns are considered id.vars, which in this case are columns [CDR3.aa, V.name, ...]. title: One function to visualise them all — vis
text: List available visualisations different kinds data. Basic analysis: Exploratory analysis results (repExplore) - see vis.immunr_exp_vol; Clonality statistics (repClonality) - see vis.immunr_homeo. Overlaps public clonotypes: Overlaps (repOverlap) using heatmaps, circos plots, polar area plots - see vis.immunr_ov_matrix; Overlap clustering (repOverlapAnalysis) - see vis.immunr_hclust; Repertoire incremental overlaps (repOverlap) - see vis.immunr_inc_overlap; Public repertoire abundance (pubRep) - vis vis.immunr_public_repertoire. Gene usage: Gene usage statistics (geneUsage) using bar plots, box plots - see vis.immunr_gene_usage; Gene usage distances (geneUsageAnalysis) using heatmaps, circos plots, polar area plots - see vis.immunr_ov_matrix; Gene usage clustering (geneUsageAnalysis) - see vis.immunr_hclust. Diversity estimation: Diversity estimations (repDiversity) - see vis.immunr_chao1. BCR analysis: Clonal tree (repClonalFamily) - see vis.clonal_family vis.clonal_family_tree. Advanced analysis: Repertoire dynamics (trackClonotypes) - see vis.immunr_dynamics; Sequence logo plots amino acid distributions (kmer_profile) - see vis_seqlogo; Kmers distributions (getKmers) - see vis.immunr_kmer_table; Mutation networks (mutationNetwork) - Work Progress vis.immunr_mutation_network; CDR3 amino acid properties, e.g., biophysical (cdrProp) - Work Progress vis.immunr_cdr_prop. Additionaly, provide wrapper functions visualisations common data types: data frames matrices using heatmaps - see vis_heatmap vis_heatmap2; data frames matrices using circos plots - see vis_circos.

code: # Load an example data that comes with immunarch data(immdata)  # Make the data smaller in order to speed up the examples immdata$data <- immdata$data[c(1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9)] immdata$meta <- immdata$meta[c(1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9), ]  # Option 1 # Choose the first 10 amino acid clonotype sequences # from the first repertoire to track tc <- trackClonotypes(immdata$data, list(1, 10), .col = "aa") # Choose the first 20 nucleotide clonotype sequences # and their V genes from the "MS1" repertoire to track tc <- trackClonotypes(immdata$data, list("MS1", 20), .col = "nt+v")  # Option 2 # Choose clonotypes with amino acid sequences "CASRGLITDTQYF" or "CSASRGSPNEQYF" tc <- trackClonotypes(immdata$data, c("CASRGLITDTQYF", "CSASRGSPNEQYF"), .col = "aa")  # Option 3 # Choose the first 10 clonotypes from the first repertoire # with amino acid sequences and V segments target <- immdata$data[[1]] %>%   select(CDR3.aa, V.name) %>%   head(10) tc <- trackClonotypes(immdata$data, target)  # Visualise the output regardless of the chosen option # Therea are three way to visualise it, regulated by the .plot argument vis(tc, .plot = "smooth") #> Warning: id.vars and measure.vars are internally guessed when both are 'NULL'. All non-numeric/integer/logical type columns are considered id.vars, which in this case are columns [CDR3.aa, V.name, ...]. Consider providing at least one of 'id' or 'measure' vars in future.  vis(tc, .plot = "area") #> Warning: id.vars and measure.vars are internally guessed when both are 'NULL'. All non-numeric/integer/logical type columns are considered id.vars, which in this case are columns [CDR3.aa, V.name, ...]. Consider providing at least one of 'id' or 'measure' vars in future.  vis(tc, .plot = "line") #> Warning: id.vars and measure.vars are internally guessed when both are 'NULL'. All non-numeric/integer/logical type columns are considered id.vars, which in this case are columns [CDR3.aa, V.name, ...]. Consider providing at least one of 'id' or 'measure' vars in future.   # Visualising timepoints # First, we create an additional column in the metadata with randomly choosen timepoints: immdata$meta$Timepoint <- sample(1:length(immdata$data)) immdata$meta #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   Sample  ID    Sex     Age Status Lane  Timepoint #>   <chr>   <chr> <chr> <dbl> <chr>  <chr>     <int> #> 1 A2-i129 C1    M        11 C      A             3 #> 2 A2-i131 C2    M         9 C      A             2 #> 3 A2-i133 C4    M        16 C      A             1 #> 4 MS1     MS1   M        12 MS     C             5 #> 5 MS2     MS2   M        30 MS     C             6 #> 6 MS3     MS3   M         8 MS     C             4 # Next, we create a vector with samples in the right order, # according to the "Timepoint" column (from smallest to greatest): sample_order <- order(immdata$meta$Timepoint) # Sanity check: timepoints are following the right order: immdata$meta$Timepoint[sample_order] #> [1] 1 2 3 4 5 6 # Samples, sorted by the timepoints: immdata$meta$Sample[sample_order] #> [1] "A2-i133" "A2-i131" "A2-i129" "MS3"     "MS1"     "MS2"     # And finally, we visualise the data: vis(tc, .order = sample_order) #> Warning: id.vars and measure.vars are internally guessed when both are 'NULL'.
